authors: Tessa Bijelic; Ambrosina Michelotti; Rosaria Bucci; Daniela Del Sorbo; EwaCarin Ekberg; Birgitta Häggman‐Henrikson
fulltext_exclusion_reason: fewer than two domains substantively covered
pain_condition_detail: Temporomandibular disorder (TMD): pain in masticatory muscles and temporomandibular joints.
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS as background framing and intervention rationale, but does not operationalize it. BPS is mentioned in the introduction and discussion to justify multimodal self-management, but the review itself does not code or measure BPS domains.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper mentions that psychosocial function correlates with TMD symptoms but does not specify a pathway. No other cross-domain relations are articulated.
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper advocates a biopsychosocial approach but defines the model only in terms of emotional, cognitive, and behavioural factors, omitting biological and social domains
conceptual_tensions_2: The paper claims BPS supports multimodal treatment but does not integrate domains in its own analysis
synthesis_note: This umbrella review uses BPS as background framing and intervention rationale but does not operationalize it. The psychological domain is elaborated (patient education, CBT, behavioural therapy, kinesiophobia, catastrophising), while biological and social domains are minimal. No cross-domain integration is present. The BPS definition omits social factors.
coding_rationale: Typology is pseudo_bps because BPS language is used but only psychological content is elaborated. Triadic integration is none because no cross-domain relations are articulated beyond a single correlation.

citation: Bijelic et al. (2025), Journal of Oral Rehabilitation
title: Self‐Management Therapies for Temporomandibular Disorders—Evidence From Systematic Reviews
authors: Tessa Bijelic; Ambrosina Michelotti; Rosaria Bucci; Daniela Del Sorbo; EwaCarin Ekberg; Birgitta Häggman‐Henrikson
icd11_pain_category: chronic secondary headache or orofacial pain
pain_condition_detail: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD), described as orofacial pain involving masticatory muscles and temporomandibular joints.
context_note: Included SRs were conducted in the United Kingdom, Brazil, Canada, China, Germany, Italy, and Japan.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS mainly as a justification for patient-centred, multimodal self-management. It operationalizes BPS through intervention components (patient education, behavioural/CBT, jaw exercises) and outcomes (pain, mouth opening, quality of life), with no explicit three-domain mechanism.
integration_mechanism_summary: One behavioural mechanism is proposed: behavioural therapy is said to target jaw-system rehabilitation by identifying, monitoring and avoiding disadvantageous behaviours and reinforcing advantageous behaviours. No explicit three-domain mechanism is proposed.
emergent_labels_10: disc displacement with or without reduction
conceptual_tensions_1: BPS language is used to support self-management, but the paper does not turn the model into measured variables or a triadic mechanism
conceptual_tensions_2: Self-management is described as multimodal, yet the heterogeneity of components makes it difficult to attribute effects to specific parts
conceptual_tensions_3: Evidence is reported as beneficial, but certainty is often low or very low and methodological concerns are frequent
conceptual_tensions_4: Patient education, behavioural therapy and CBT are sometimes grouped as psychological interventions, creating conceptual overlap
conceptual_tensions_5: Quality of life and adverse effects are recommended as important outcomes but are less often reported in the included reviews
additional_observations_1: No psychological instruments are named for constructs such as kinesiophobia, pain catastrophising, coping or CBT outcomes
additional_observations_2: DC/TMD and RDC/TMD are used as diagnostic classification systems, not as measures of biopsychosocial constructs
additional_observations_3: Included systematic reviews were conducted in seven countries, but no country-specific social mechanisms are analysed
additional_observations_4: The paper does not name family, cultural, socioeconomic, compensation, stigma, or social determinant factors
additional_observations_5: Future research recommendations emphasize children and adolescents, quality of life, and adverse effects
additional_observations_6: The review reports 53% overlap of primary studies across included systematic reviews
synthesis_note: The paper uses BPS mainly to justify patient-centred, multimodal self-management for TMD. Biological content is mostly TMD anatomy, pain/function outcomes and jaw exercises; psychological content is education/behavioural/CBT and related constructs. Social content is limited to demographics, healthcare professionals and patient-centred framing. It does not propose a three-domain mechanism.
coding_rationale: Multifactorial typology: all domains appear, but social content is thin and cross-domain claims are mostly intervention-based rather than mechanistic.

citation: Bijelic et al. (2025), Journal of Oral Rehabilitation
title: Self‐Management Therapies for Temporomandibular Disorders—Evidence From Systematic Reviews
authors: Tessa Bijelic; Ambrosina Michelotti; Rosaria Bucci; Daniela Del Sorbo; EwaCarin Ekberg; Birgitta Häggman‐Henrikson
pain_condition_detail: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD): musculoskeletal pain and jaw dysfunction in orofacial region
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale
bps_operationalization_summary: The BPS model is used as a conceptual framework to justify multimodal self-management interventions for TMD, but the review does not operationalize the model into specific variables or measures. Instead, it uses BPS language to frame the need for comprehensive treatment approaches.
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between invoking the biopsychosocial model as a comprehensive framework while only substantively addressing biological and psychological domains, leaving the social dimension absent from the evidence synthesis
conceptual_tensions_2: Ambiguity in defining self-management therapy components - the paper notes 'there is no clearly defined distinction between the therapeutic content of self-management therapy components', creating measurement and conceptual clarity issues
additional_observations_1: The review is an umbrella review of systematic reviews, not a primary systematic review, which limits its ability to extract primary data on BPS integration
additional_observations_2: Patient education is positioned as foundational to self-management, with the paper noting it 'constitutes a basic and essential part in managing TMD' and is 'one of several evaluated therapies'
additional_observations_3: The review identifies methodological limitations in primary studies (low certainty evidence, high risk of bias) that constrain confidence in BPS-related findings
synthesis_note: This umbrella review of TMD self-management therapies uses the biopsychosocial label to frame multifactorial treatment approaches but substantively covers only biological (TMD pathology, jaw exercises) and psychological (education, CBT, behavioral therapy) domains. The social domain is entirely absent from the evidence synthesis. Psychological concepts are well-developed with multiple intervention components and outcomes, while biological content is minimal. The BPS model serves as background framing and intervention rationale rather than an operationalized framework. This exemplifies 'multifactorial' typology where all three domains are conceptually present but only two are substantively integrated.
coding_rationale: BPS typology is 'multifactorial' because biological and psychological domains are substantively covered while social is absent. Integration is 'none' for all cross-domain pairs. Psychological domain scored 'elaborated' due to multiple named constructs and intervention components. Biological scored 'mentioned' with only TMD pathology and jaw exercises named. Social domain genuinely absent despite BPS label usage.

concept_relations_03_relation_verbatim: Counselling is one recurring behavioural therapy component that usually forms part of self‐care interventions for TMD. In the primary studies, counselling included advice about relaxation techniques, deep breathing, sleep hygiene, therapeutic exercises, thermal therapy, self‐massage and a pain‐free diet. Since there is no clearly defined distinction between the therapeutic content of self‐management therapy components, counselling frequently serves as a therapeutic bridge between behavioural therapy and patient education.
